title: Pipe coupling
use_case: Pipe prefabrication: a threaded steel coupling (1 inch pipe size, about 40 mm across and 45 mm long) sits loosely on the threaded stub of a pipe spool that stands upright. Push it onto the thread start and turn it on until it is hand-tight (about 3 N m), never over 8 N m.
headline: A two-tool head completes the task in 8 of 8 runs; the best single off-the-shelf tool in 0 of 8 runs.

plan.title: Pipe coupling tightening
plan.description: A threaded coupling sits on a pipe stub; insert it to the thread start then tighten clockwise to hand‑tight torque.
assumptions: The coupling outer diameter is about 40 mm and length 45 mm.
Thread pitch is 1.5 mm, typical for 1‑inch pipe threads.
Seating depth is chamfer plus 3 mm.

steps.description: Push the coupling onto the thread start until it seats on the chamfer.
caveats: Threads are an approximation: a helical joint with a torque ramp; no thread flanks, cross-threading or galling. A screen, not a promise.

steps.description: Turn the coupling clockwise to hand‑tight torque.
